newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: INTERVIEW-Investec casts eyes globally.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Investec casts eyes globally.

text.p: Investec Ltd, a South African financial services firm whose recent history reads like a shopping list of acquisitions, is on the prowl for more buys on its home turf, in southern Africa and offshore.

Chairman Hugh Herman said in an interview that the group, which offers private banking and investment services to high net worth individuals, professionals and corporates, was looking for opportunities in Australia, the United States and Zimbabwe.
"Our intention is to get going in Australia although in what form we are not sure yet. If we can't accquire anything we will probably grassroot something there," Herman said.

He said that Investec had already opened an office there, employing one person who was on the lookout for potential buys. Application had also been made for a banking licence which should be granted shortly.
One attraction of the Australian market was the high number of South African expatriates living there, following a flood of emigration by mostly white professionals in recent years.

The United States, where Investec's trade finance unit Reichman's Ltd is already represented, was another potential growth area following the success of the link with firm Gerber Northeast Inc. "It looks like we will make a little profit there this year," Herman said.

Plans are afoot to start distributing South African securities from New York and a one-man office had also been set up there. "Again he is looking for a small acquisition, but it is not so easy in the U.S.," Herman said.

Investec, which has shown compound share earnings growth in excess of 29 percent over the past 10 years, has also set up shop in areas closer to home. It recently bought a small stake in an Angolan-based Portuguese bank and launched asset management operations in Namibia. It is already in Botswana and Swaziland.
Herman said that Investec was keen to achieve a greater presence throughout the southern African region.
"We certainly are looking at Zimbabwe...we think that there are opportunities there and in Zambia and we will get to them one by one," he said.
Despite spreading its focus, Investec's eye was still firmly on Britain, its biggest international operation.

Its presence there dates back to 1992 when it bought London-based Allied Trust Bank, recently renamed Investec Bank (UK) Ltd. Other British buys include Clive Discount Co Ltd in 1995, the moneybroking operations of Cazenove & Co (UK) and stockbroking and portfolio management firm Carr Sheppards.
"The UK still remains our focal point...We think there are a lot of opportunities there both for organic growth and acquisition," Herman said.
Investec also owns a controlling share in Israel General Bank, that country's eighth largest bank.
Herman said that the group planned to establish closer ties with Dutch asset management and stockbroking firm, Insinger SA.

"It is conceivable that in the not too distant future we will be able to find a formula whereby we will be able to merge certainly the international operations of our bank with their operations," he said.

On its homefront Investec has also snapped up a range of businesses, moving strongly into stockbroking following the deregulation of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in 1995 and the purchase of J. Solms & Co and more recently Fergusson Bros.
Herman said that despite the group's widespread activities it did not have an appetite for the branch-based retail market.
"Today in our field it is no longer necessary. That whole bricks and mortar concept is going to be supplanted by electronics and telephone banking."
He said Investec was launching a credit card in September.
Investec's shares have risen by about 62 percent since the start of the year, hitting a record high of 185 rand on June 30.
-- Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
